description: Jason abandons Medea for a princess. She kills their children. Euripides creates a terrifying, intelligent, foreign heroine: passion becomes reasoning.

hero.hook: A betrayed woman. A cold calculation. The Greek theater would no longer forget this shock.

blocks.text: In **431 BC**, in Athens, **Euripides**, one of the three great authors of Greek tragedy, presented **Medea**. **Jason**, Greek hero and leader of the , a legendary expedition aboard the ship Argo, pledged loyalty to **Medea**, a magician who helped him take the **Golden Fleece**. In **Corinth**, he leaves her to marry the king's daughter. [[Argonautes]]

Medea doesn't just cry. She plans absolute revenge. Euripides places at the center a woman who speaks, calculates and chooses the irreparable. The piece shocks from its creation. It remains one of the most feared tragedies in the repertoire.

Alongside , first of the three great tragedians and author of the Oresteia, and , author of Oedipus Rex, Euripides explores interiority. His characters doubt, contradict themselves, justify the unjustifiable. The Athenian public sometimes found him too cynical. Later, he would be read as a genius of dramatic psychology. blocks.text: Medea is not a silent fury. She **argues**. That's what's scary. Euripides gives him brilliant speeches on injustice done to women, on betrayal, on shame. The monster speaks with disturbing lucidity.

sections.title: Euripides, the most “modern” of the three

blocks.text: Medea is  in the eyes of the Greeks. The term refers to anyone who does not speak Greek. Here, she is a woman from **Colchis**, a distant region on the Black Sea. She betrayed her people for Jason. When he repudiates her, she loses status, protection, future.  becomes explosive here: the excluded person knows the rules better than the masters of the game. [[Barbarous]] [[The figure of the stranger in Greek tragedy]]
Jason owes him everything: without Medea's spells, no Golden Fleece. Euripides insists: the “civilized” man behaves ungratefully, while the foreigner pays the price for her broken loyalty.

sections.title: The stranger whose pact is broken

blocks.text: Medea hesitates. She loves her sons. Then she decides: to kill them is to strike Jason in the heart, where Greek family honor is most sensitive. The , the irascible part of the soul, seat of anger and courage, wins. But in a lucid speech. This is not a silent “stroke of madness”. It’s a cold calculation, chosen after a heartbreaking monologue. [[Thumos]]

At the end, a : Medea escapes on a winged chariot sent by her grandfather the **Sun**, the god **Helios**. It is a theatrical process where a divine force unravels the action. No immediate punishment. The uneasiness remains in the room. The audience leaves confused, with no simple moral answer. [[Deus ex machina]]

sections.title: Killing your children: reason versus passion?

blocks.text: From **Seneca**, Latin author of tragedies, to **Pasolini**, Italian filmmaker, from **Crow**, 17th century French playwright, to contemporary stages, Medea returns. We read about revenge, feminism, colonization, the rage of abandonment. Euripides does not excuse infanticide. It forces us to hear the voice of the person who commits it.

Euripides also suggests the political cost of the act: Medea hits Jason, but she also hits the future of the city by destroying the lineage. The **choir**, a group of women from Corinth who comment on the action, hesitates between compassion and horror. This ambivalence is the strength of the piece: we understand without exonerating, we shudder without being able to look away.

**Medea** by Euripides shows that a private injustice can become an absolute catastrophe. The betrayed foreigner plots her revenge, and the Greek theater discovers a heroine that is impossible to put down.
